# Implement block: Breathing Gap Grid (React Native)

You are adding the "Breathing Gap Grid" block from Native Cook to the user's React Native app. The block already exists as working code. Your job is to bring it into this project faithfully, not to write a new one that looks similar.

## The block

A wall of square tiles on a black screen in four columns centred on it, the outer two running half off its edges: eighty editorial photos (portraits, busts and plaster casts, ceramics, dried flowers, fashion, sneakers, chairs and still lifes, a dune) mixed with seven squares of set type (a white "A" on cobalt, a red "N" on cream, "ROOM" three times in white on black, "Hi." in black on white, "LOOK" twice in cobalt on white, a white "O" on red, "GAP" in black on cream), dealt so that the same tile never appears within eight cells of itself. Each photo darkens softly towards its bottom edge. Tiny capitals sit in the corners: "Studio Notes", "Frames" and a live readout of the columns and the gap ("4 col · Gap 14 pt") along the top, "Pinch", "Drag" and "Tap" along the bottom. Opened out, the wall zooms out to eight whole columns of small tiles with even margins at both edges, and the rows part around a darkened lane across the middle where "Room to breathe" sits in spaced capitals between two thin rules. A tapped tile lifts out to nearly the full width over the blurred, dimmed wall, with a glow in its own colour beneath it and its note and title underneath.

**Motion.** On arrival the tiles grow in from 55% of their size and fade in, rippling out from the middle of the screen over 0.7 s, each over 0.65 s, while the columns start drifting five times faster and settle to their own pace over 1.8 s; each photo, fetched at 400 px square, fades in over 0.45 s once it has loaded, and the labels fade in after 0.45 s. The columns drift upward on their own at 0.22 to 0.38 cells per second, each at its own speed and from its own phase. Closed up the columns sit 30% of the screen's width apart and a tile fills 88% of its cell; opened out the grid zooms out evenly about the middle of the screen until eight columns fill the width with a tile filling 56% of its cell and the margins at the edges as wide as the gaps, and a selection haptic ticks each time another pair of columns comes into view under the fingers. Pinching in by 2.4 times goes all the way, following at a quarter of the pull past either end; on release the pinch's speed carries the gap 0.15 s ahead and a spring (duration 520 ms, damping ratio 0.86) settles it on whichever end is nearer, with a light haptic. As the gap opens the rows within 150 pt of the middle part by up to 26 pt either side, tiles whose edge comes within 6 pt of the line fade out, and a 120 pt lane behind it darkens; past 35% of the way the letters of "Room to breathe" arrive one after another, each rising 12 pt out of a 5 pt blur, and two rules draw out from it to 20 pt from the edges. Dragging moves the whole wall with the finger and lets it glide on with its speed (deceleration 0.997). Tapping a tile fetches it again at 1080 px, fading the sharper copy in over the small one when it arrives, and lifts it out of its cell on a spring (duration 520 ms, damping ratio 0.88) with a light haptic: it grows to the width less 24 pt a side and rises to 42% of the screen while the wall behind it blurs by up to 10 pt, dims by 80% and slows to a stop, and a glow in the tile's colour spreads 34 pt below it; its note and title ride just below it, rising 16 pt as they fade in over the last 45% of the way. An open tile follows the finger in both directions, shrinking by up to 45% as it is pulled down and resisting at 30% when pushed up, while its title fades and the wall sharpens and brightens back; a release faster than 650 pt/s downward or more than 110 pt down returns it to its cell with a light haptic, otherwise it springs back to the middle (duration 460 ms, damping ratio 0.9), both carrying the finger's speed. A tap anywhere closes it too. The top and bottom edges darken over 96 pt so the labels stay legible. The self-playing demo opens the gap at 1.4 s and closes it at 4.8 s, each over 1.2 s on an ease-in-out curve (0.77, 0, 0.175, 1), lifts out the photo in the second column nearest the middle at 6.6 s, puts it back at 8.8 s and repeats every 11 s. A touch stops it for 3 s, longer while a tile is open. Under reduced motion the columns stand still, the tiles fade in without growing, the demo does not play, a drag does not glide, the letters fade without rising or blurring, the wall does not blur, and the gap and the open tile change in 200 ms without springs.

## Reference source

The block is built and running in the Native Cook source repository. Each link below is a file on GitHub. To read one as plain text, replace `https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/` with `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/` in its address.

### Demo (start here)

- [index.tsx](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/react-native/src/blocks/gestures/breathing-gap-grid/index.tsx)

### Files of the block

- [BreathingGapGrid.tsx](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/react-native/src/blocks/gestures/breathing-gap-grid/BreathingGapGrid.tsx)

### Packages

- `@shopify/react-native-skia`
- `expo-haptics`
- `expo-status-bar`
- `react-native-gesture-handler`
- `react-native-reanimated`
- `react-native-safe-area-context`
- `react-native-worklets`

The versions the block was built with are in [react-native/package.json](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/react-native/package.json).

## Your instructions

_Anything specific to this app goes here: where the block should appear, what to rename, what to change. Left empty, integrate the block as it is._

## How to work

Work like an experienced React Native engineer joining an existing project: learn the app first, read only what you need, decide early how the block fits, then integrate it with as little disruption as possible. Take the steps in order.

**Done means** the block is reachable in the user's app and behaves like the reference on iOS or Android: a simulator, an emulator or a device. A browser is never proof. Do not open the app on the web to check it, not even when the mobile build fails.

**Fidelity.** Bring over the real implementation. Keep its structure, colours, sizes, timings and easing. Change only what this project requires and what "Your instructions" ask for.

If you already learned this project earlier in the conversation, reuse what you know and skip step 2. Learn it again only if the project changed or something you need is missing.

### 1. Check where you are

- You need the project's files and a terminal. If this prompt was pasted into a chat that has neither, stop and say so: it has to be run by a coding agent opened on the project.
- Confirm the project is a React Native app, Expo or bare. If it is something else, stop, say what you found, and do not create a new app inside it unless the instructions ask for one.

### 2. Learn the host app

- Expo (managed or prebuild) or bare React Native, and the versions of React Native and the Expo SDK.
- The package manager, and how the app is started: Expo Go, a development build, or `react-native run-ios` / `run-android`.
- Navigation: Expo Router, React Navigation, something else, or a single screen. Find how a screen is added today.
- Conventions: TypeScript or not, path aliases, how styles are written, where components and screens live.
- Which of the block's packages are already installed, and at which versions.

### 3. Read the block

- Open the demo, then each file it imports. The list above names every file of the block, so you do not have to guess.
- The demo is how the source repository shows the block. Bring over what the demo renders, not the repository's gallery. Anything listed under "Used by the demo only" stays behind.
- Read the block's props and their defaults. The demo may switch on an option that makes the block play by itself for a recording (for example `autoPlay`). Keep the option; leave it off in the user's app unless asked.

### 4. Decide the fit

- Compare the block's packages with the host's. Install what is missing with the project's own tool (`npx expo install …` in an Expo app, so versions match its SDK).
- A package with native code needs a new native build, and Expo Go only runs the modules it ships with. Say so before you install one, and say which build the user will need.
- If the host is on older versions and an API differs, adapt the block's code to the host. Do not upgrade the host's React Native, Expo SDK or animation libraries without asking.
- Put the files where this app keeps its components. Ask only when two places are equally reasonable and the choice matters.

### 5. Bring it in

- Copy the block's files, keep their names, and rewrite imports to this project's paths and aliases.
- Copy its images and fonts with it, and load fonts the way the project already does.
- Keep reduced-motion handling, haptics and accessibility labels as they are in the source.
- Mount the block where the instructions say. With no instructions, add a screen or route named after the block and make it reachable the way the app's other screens are.

### 6. Run it

- Typecheck and lint with the project's own commands and fix what the block introduced.
- Run the app on the user's usual mobile target and use the block: every state, every gesture, and once with reduced motion on.
- If the simulator, the emulator or the native build fails, report the error and ask how to continue. Do not fall back to the web.

### 7. Report

- Files added and changed, packages installed, and whether a new native build is needed.
- How to reach the block in the app.
- Anything that differs from the reference, and why.
